project_status: Educational research prototype — not a clinical decision-support device
scope_note: Selected landmark trials; intentionally not a systematic review or exhaustive database. Enrollment EF thresholds and primary endpoints vary across studies.

studies.title: Empagliflozin in Heart Failure with a Preserved Ejection Fraction

population.summary: Adults with symptomatic NYHA class II–IV heart failure and LVEF >40%.
population.additional_criteria: With or without diabetes; usual background HF therapy.

primary_outcomes.name: First cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure

studies.interpretation: The primary composite outcome favored empagliflozin, driven mainly by fewer heart-failure hospitalizations. A significant reduction in cardiovascular mortality alone was not established.
cautions: This enrollment criterion includes a broad EF spectrum, not only LVEF ≥50%.
Composite event rates and time-to-first-event estimates should not be compared directly with recurrent-event rate ratios.

reference.short_citation: Anker et al., N Engl J Med (2021)

curation.source_basis: Primary trial abstract and bibliographic PubMed record

studies.title: Dapagliflozin in Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction

population.summary: Adults with symptomatic heart failure and LVEF >40%, including some with previously reduced EF that had improved.
population.additional_criteria: Structural heart disease and elevated natriuretic peptides; with or without type 2 diabetes.

primary_outcomes.name: First worsening heart failure (hospitalization or urgent visit) or cardiovascular death

studies.interpretation: Dapagliflozin lowered the risk of the primary composite of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death. Cardiovascular death alone did not show a statistically clear reduction.
cautions: The endpoint includes urgent HF visits, unlike some other trials.
The trial enrolled mildly reduced and preserved EF, and some improved-EF patients.

reference.short_citation: Solomon et al., N Engl J Med (2022)

curation.source_basis: Primary trial abstract and bibliographic PubMed record

studies.title: Angiotensin-Neprilysin Inhibition in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction

population.summary: Patients with NYHA class II–IV heart failure, LVEF ≥45%, elevated natriuretic peptides, and structural heart disease.
population.additional_criteria: Symptomatic heart failure with elevated natriuretic peptide levels.

primary_outcomes.name: Total heart-failure hospitalizations and cardiovascular death
primary_outcomes.result_text: 894 vs 1,009 total primary events; rate ratio 0.87 (95% CI 0.75–1.01), p=0.06.

studies.interpretation: The prespecified primary composite did not meet statistical significance in the overall study population.
cautions: The comparator was valsartan, not placebo.
Exploratory subgroup signals should not be presented as overall trial success.

reference.short_citation: Solomon et al., N Engl J Med (2019)

curation.source_basis: Primary trial abstract and bibliographic PubMed record

studies.title: Spironolactone for Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction

population.summary: Patients with symptomatic heart failure and LVEF ≥45%.
population.additional_criteria: Trial participants met criteria for symptomatic HFpEF enrollment.

primary_outcomes.name: Cardiovascular death, aborted cardiac arrest, or HF hospitalization

studies.interpretation: No statistically significant reduction in the primary composite; hospitalization for heart failure alone was lower, while hyperkalemia was more frequent.
cautions: The primary composite was not statistically significant.
Serum potassium and renal function safety findings matter when interpreting this trial.

reference.short_citation: Pitt et al., N Engl J Med (2014)

curation.source_basis: Primary trial abstract and bibliographic PubMed record

studies.title: Semaglutide in Patients with Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Obesity

population.summary: Patients with HFpEF and obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²); LVEF ≥45% under the trial eligibility criteria.
population.additional_criteria: Obesity-associated HFpEF; this original STEP-HFpEF trial excluded diabetes.

primary_outcomes.name: Change in KCCQ clinical summary score at 52 weeks
primary_outcomes.result_text: Mean change +16.6 vs +8.7 points; estimated difference +7.8 points (95% CI 4.8–10.9), p<0.001.

primary_outcomes.name: Percentage change in body weight at 52 weeks
primary_outcomes.result_text: Mean change −13.3% vs −2.6%; difference −10.7 percentage points (95% CI −11.9 to −9.4), p<0.001.

studies.interpretation: Semaglutide improved patient-reported symptoms/physical limitations and reduced weight in obesity-associated HFpEF. This trial was not primarily designed to establish mortality benefit.
cautions: Its two co-primary outcomes differ substantially from clinical-event endpoints in other trials.
The 529-participant trial studied a selected obesity-related phenotype and excluded diabetes.

reference.short_citation: Kosiborod et al., N Engl J Med (2023)

curation.source_basis: Primary trial abstract and bibliographic PubMed record

studies.title: Finerenone in Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction

population.summary: Patients with symptomatic heart failure and LVEF ≥40%.
population.additional_criteria: On usual therapy; included participants with mildly reduced or preserved EF.

intervention.name: Finerenone
intervention.dose: Up to 20 or 40 mg once daily, depending on protocol criteria

primary_outcomes.name: Total worsening HF events and cardiovascular death
primary_outcomes.result_text: 1,083 vs 1,283 total primary events; rate ratio 0.84 (95% CI 0.74–0.95), p=0.007.

studies.interpretation: Finerenone reduced the rate of the recurrent-event composite outcome. Hyperkalemia occurred more often; cardiovascular death considered alone was not significantly reduced.
cautions: Includes patients with LVEF ≥40%, not solely conventional HFpEF.
Recurrent-event rate ratio is not interchangeable with a time-to-first-event hazard ratio.

reference.short_citation: Solomon et al., N Engl J Med (2024)

curation.source_basis: Primary trial abstract and bibliographic PubMed record
